correctness.rationale: For p,q≥3 every nonclique triple has a repeated coordinate. Up to graph symmetries, three exhaustive cases yield an induced five-vertex path, an induced four-vertex path, or an induced three-vertex path. All consecutive cell pairs differ in both coordinates and all nonconsecutive pairs share a coordinate, proving no chords. Conversely a clique cannot have three vertices on an induced path. Hence exactly all ≤2-subsets and cliques of size ≥3 qualify. Counting k-cliques by row subset, column subset and bijection yields C(p,k)C(q,k)k!. Inclusion-maximality follows by extending every edge to a triangle and every submaximum clique to larger size; nonedges are maximal. Original-graph exhaustive induced-path enumeration on (3,3),(3,4),(3,5),(4,4) matches both polynomials. Finite tests do not establish the general case; the explicit exhaustive proof does.

Brešar et al. study strongly 2-monophonic graphs and prove a sufficient cycle condition, but no theorem there identifies categorical products K_p×K_q as strongly 2-monophonic; their explicit Hamming examples use Cartesian adjacency and are the *complements* of the present graphs.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons found no antecedent covering the all-cardinality or maximal monophonic-position census on categorical products K_p×K_q. A foundational monophonic-position theorem says induced subgraphs on position sets are unions of cliques; it does not force a single clique on this family. The lower general-position number and general-position polynomial on the identical graph use shortest paths, so neither implies the stronger induced-path classification. Recent monophonic product literature is about Cartesian and lexicographic graph products, which have different adjacency. Brešar et al. (arXiv:2509.18784) introduced strongly 2-monophonic coverage and classified other graph families, but do not establish this property or position-set enumeration for categorical products K_p×K_q. Indexed mathematical-finding and recoverable claim comparisons were likewise not equivalent. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a guarantee against unindexed work.
residual_risks: A less-indexed journal article, thesis or terminology variant could independently contain this family-specific characterization or the same polynomial. No claim of exhaustive global uniqueness is made.
General-position and monophonic-position terminology is sometimes conflated in abstracts; detailed new citations could alter a future priority assessment.

value.rationale: This is a natural vertex-transitive graph-product family already studied for related path-position invariants; the 2025 literature asks which vertex-transitive graphs are strongly 2-monophonic. An explicit three-case induced-path witness theorem yields a complete infinite-family classification, both the all-subset enumerator and maximal-set enumerator, and the sharp maximality spectrum {2,min(p,q)}. It demonstrates unbounded separation between the smallest and largest maximal monophonic configurations, and between monophonic versus geodesic position when p=3 and q grows. The central path-witness lemma, not just binomial arithmetic, supplies substantial structure beyond routine parameter recomputation.
